record.paper_title: Open problems on graph eigenvalues studied with AutoGraphiX
record.original_question: Let s(G) = lambda_1(G) - lambda_n(G) be the spectral spread of a connected graph G on n >= 3 vertices. Is it true that s(G) <= sqrt(4qn - 3q^2 - 2q + 1), where q = ceil(2n/3), with equality if and only if G is the complete split graph CS(n,q), meaning the graph whose vertex set is partitioned into a clique of size q and an independent set of size n-q = floor(n/3), with every clique vertex adjacent to every independent-set vertex?

evidence.quote: The problem of finding the maximum value of s(G) among the class of connected graphs of given order n is an open problem.

Conjecture 3.1' Let G be a connected graph on n >= 3 vertices. Then s(G) <= sqrt(4qn - 3q^2 - 2q + 1) with equality if and only if G is the complete split graph CS(n, q) with an independent set of size n - q = floor(n/3) and a clique of size q = ceil(2n/3).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a simple connected graph $G$ on $n\ge 3$ vertices, let $\lambda_1(G)\ge \lambda_2(G)\ge\cdots\ge \lambda_n(G)$ denote the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix, and define the spectral spread
$$s(G)=\lambda_1(G)-\lambda_n(G).$$
For integers $n\ge 3$ and $1\le q\le n-1$, let $CS(n,q)$ denote the complete split graph: the graph on $n$ vertices whose vertex set is partitioned into a clique of size $q$ and an independent set of size $n-q$, with every vertex of the clique adjacent to every vertex of the independent set. Set $q=\lceil 2n/3\rceil$ (so $n-q=\lfloor n/3\rfloor$).

Prove or disprove: for every connected graph $G$ on $n\ge 3$ vertices,
$$s(G)\le \sqrt{4qn-3q^2-2q+1},$$
with equality if and only if $G\cong CS(n,q)$.
artifact.status_search_result: Breen, Riasanovsky, Tait, and Urschel ("Maximum spread of graphs and bipartite graphs", arXiv:2109.03129, Comm. AMS 2022) proved the long-standing Gregory–Hershkowitz–Kirkland conjecture that the spread-maximizing $n$-vertex graph is the join of a clique of size $\lfloor 2n/3\rfloor$ and an independent set of size $\lceil n/3\rceil$ — a complete split graph — for all sufficiently large $n$. The conjecture remains open for all $n$, so the bound and equality case stated above are established only asymptotically.

status_evidence.title: Maximum spread of graphs and bipartite graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Resolves the Gregory–Hershkowitz–Kirkland conjecture: for all positive integers n, the n-vertex graph maximizing spread is the join of a clique and an independent set with floor(2n/3) and ceil(n/3) vertices; proved for all n sufficiently large.
status_evidence.claim: The spread-maximizing complete split graph conjecture is proved for all sufficiently large n.

status_evidence.title: MAXIMUM SPREAD OF GRAPHS AND BIPARTITE GRAPHS
status_evidence.snippet: Pair of 20-year-old conjectures of Gregory, Hershkowitz, and Kirkland regarding the spread of graphs ... proved for all n sufficiently large.
status_evidence.claim: Proof currently established only for sufficiently large n.
